clues.name: Police Lockdown
clues.context: Officer Reyes sealed the mansion at 8:15 PM. Nobody in or out since.
clues.inspectorDescription: Doors sealed at 8:15 PM. Officer Reyes does not negotiate. I checked.

clues.name: PR Disaster
clues.context: The Manager, Chip Sterling, is furious that a missing animal is generating terrible press for his client.
clues.inspectorDescription: Chip Sterling hates animals and loves percentages. Strong feelings. No evidence either way.

clues.name: D. Marsh - 6:30 PM
clues.context: The sign-in book by the entrance. One entry reads: 'D. Marsh - 6:30 PM.'
clues.inspectorDescription: He signed the registry at 6:30 PM. The rest of the crew trickled in after. I can hold two numbers in my head at once. Barely.

clues.name: Hallway Rumble - 7 PM
clues.context: Derek heard something heavy rattle past the bedroom around 7:00 PM. He assumed it was the dinner cart.
clues.inspectorDescription: Wheels. Rattling. Seven o'clock. He didn't look. Could have been the dinner service. Could have been anything on wheels.

clues.name: D. Marsh - 7:00 PM
clues.context: The delivery manifest lists several crew members. One signed in two acoustic cases at exactly 7:00 PM: D. Marsh.
clues.inspectorDescription: Two acoustic cases, signed in at 7:00 PM sharp. The only line on the manifest with the word 'sound-proof' in it.

clues.name: Sound-Proof Cases
clues.context: The cases are rated for complete acoustic isolation.
clues.inspectorDescription: Rated for total acoustic isolation. I pressed an ear against one for science. Nothing.

clues.name: Star's Ultimatum
clues.context: A handwritten note from Vivienne Vale to her husband: 'Derek - Rudebeak woke me up at 5AM. AGAIN. Do SOMETHING about that bird or I am calling my lawyer.'
clues.inspectorDescription: Vivienne wanted the bird 'handled.' Derek's solution arrived in a headphone box. Somebody else's didn't.

clues.name: Derek's Headphones
clues.context: A freshly opened box of top-of-the-line noise-canceling headphones. The receipt is dated yesterday.
clues.inspectorDescription: Ordered the day before the shoot. The bird drove him to it. His solution was at least legal.

clues.name: 8:00 PM Squawk
clues.context: Vivienne Vale is certain she heard Rudebeak squawk at exactly 8:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: She knows that screech anywhere, she says. Nobody actually SAW the bird after dinner.

clues.name: Broken Latch
clues.context: The cage latch was forced open with something flat and strong.
clues.inspectorDescription: Forced open with something flat and strong. And the feathers beneath the cage have long since settled.

clues.name: Hidden Speaker
clues.context: A small wireless speaker was tucked behind the cage stand, half-hidden by a fern.
clues.inspectorDescription: Taped where nobody would look unless they were cat-height. A thin cable runs from it into the wall.

clues.name: Documentary Camera
clues.context: A film crew camera on a tripod with its recording light on, positioned near the birdcage.
clues.inspectorDescription: If it filmed anything useful, Director Wexler has already watched it and said nothing.

clues.name: Vocab Ledger
clues.context: A booklet of phrases taught to Rudebeak. The entry for 'garbage slop' is crossed out with 'MAID'S FAULT' written next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: Vivienne blames Rosa for teaching Rudebeak the insult. Somebody in this house was keeping score.

clues.name: Ruined Takes
clues.context: A session log by the mixer: 'TAKE 47 - RUINED. BIRD. AGAIN.' Pages and pages of them.
clues.inspectorDescription: Forty-seven ruined takes. The handwriting gets angrier with every page.

clues.name: Wexler's Ratings
clues.context: Director Wexler sees the crisis as a documentary opportunity. He is thrilled.
clues.inspectorDescription: Not grief. Ratings. Suspiciously thrilled - or just a vulture with a lens?

clues.name: Audio Cable
clues.context: An audio cable runs from the mixing board and disappears into the wall.
clues.inspectorDescription: It leaves the mixing board and vanishes into the wall, heading west. Cables don't usually hide behind wainscoting.

clues.name: Sound Guy: D. Marsh
clues.context: The Sound Guy's name badge identifies him as D. Marsh.
clues.inspectorDescription: Badge says D. Marsh. He said 'nice cat' in a voice half an octave too high. His headphones aren't plugged into anything.

clues.name: Shot List
clues.context: The Director's shot list shows 'Rudebeak reaction shot' was cancelled, with a note in red pen: 'BETTER WITHOUT HIM?'
clues.inspectorDescription: He cancelled the bird's segment. And then wrote a very suspicious note about it in red pen.

clues.name: Rosa the Maid
clues.context: Rosa has a temper, a cleaver, and access to every room in the house.
clues.inspectorDescription: A temper, a motive, and a master key. And nobody watches the kitchen between courses.

clues.name: Insulted Cooking
clues.context: The bird publicly insulted Rosa's cooking. She wrote it down. She drew a skull next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: The bird called her paella garbage slop. In front of guests. She drew a skull. In pen.

clues.name: Rosa's Paella
clues.context: Rosa's paella is on the stove. It smells extraordinary.
clues.inspectorDescription: For the record: the paella smells incredible. Rudebeak had terrible taste in food criticism.

clues.name: Feathers in the Bin
clues.context: A bin of feathers by the prep counter. Chicken feathers - tonight's roast, plucked in-house.
clues.inspectorDescription: My heart stopped. Then I sniffed: chicken, not macaw. Rosa plucks the dinner herself. Noted, with respect.

clues.name: Dinner Cart - 7:00 PM
clues.context: The kitchen duty roster: 'R. - dinner cart to the east wing, 7:00 PM.' The east wing is where the bedrooms are.
clues.inspectorDescription: Rosa. A heavy cart. The bedroom wing. Seven o'clock. The plot thickens like a good bechamel.

clues.name: Basil the Gardener
clues.context: Basil believes caged animals should be free. He is trimming the same hedge for the fourth time.
clues.inspectorDescription: 'Animals belong in nature.' Said four times, unprompted, to a cat.

clues.name: Bent Shears
clues.context: The pruning shears show a bend consistent with forcing a metal latch.
clues.inspectorDescription: The bend in these blades fits a forced metal latch the way a paw fits a sunbeam.

clues.name: Evening Feathers
clues.context: Fresh feathers in the bird bath. Rudebeak was in the garden this evening, out of his cage.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fresh and bright, still crisp on the water. He was out here this evening, having a lovely time.

clues.name: Coco's Sighting
clues.context: Coco the Socialite saw someone hauling large black cases through the garden at about 6:45 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: 'Some crew person,' she says. She was mostly focused on her drink. The cases, though - those she remembers.

clues.name: Photo - 6:47 PM
clues.context: A timestamped pool selfie. In the blurry background, a figure hauls large cases along the garden path.
clues.inspectorDescription: Timestamped 6:47 PM. The figure is blurry. The cases are not.

clues.name: Production Schedule
clues.context: The official crew schedule assigns D. Marsh to Library audio setup at 7:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: Crew schedule, 7:00 PM: 'D. Marsh - Library (audio setup).' Schedules only mean something when people follow them.

clues.name: North Gate Locked
clues.context: Police radio confirms the north garden gate was locked all evening.
clues.inspectorDescription: Locked all evening, confirmed twice on the radio. Nobody left through the garden.

clues.name: Chip's Commission
clues.context: Chip Sterling takes fifteen percent of everything the Star earns - including the bird's documentary fee.
clues.inspectorDescription: He takes fifteen percent of the bird's earnings. A man doesn't kidnap his own commission. Probably.

clues.name: Suspected Bribery
clues.context: Rosa keeps a jar of cat treats labeled 'FOR THE CAT.' If this is a bribe, it is working.
clues.inspectorDescription: She keeps treats. For me. Specifically. I must remain objective. The treats were excellent.

clues.name: Muddy Gloves
clues.context: Basil's gloves are caked in fresh mud. He says he was planting bulbs. The flower bed agrees with him.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fresh mud, matching the freshly planted bulb bed. Suspicious hands, innocent dirt.

clues.name: Feather in the Filter
clues.context: A single bright feather floats in the pool filter. It could have blown in from anywhere.
clues.inspectorDescription: One feather, in the filter. The wind carries feathers everywhere. The pool remains a suspect in my heart, but not in this case.

finalSolveSentence: [WHO] snatched Rudebeak from the garden, sealed him inside the [WHAT] - signed in as [WHEN] - and faked the 8 PM squawk through a [HOW]. It all traces back to the [WHY].
